title: Plant and animal cells compared
canonical_question: How do plant and animal cells differ?
summary: Plant and animal cells share core parts including mitochondria.
Plant cells add a wall, a vacuole, and chloroplasts.

sections.heading: Shared machinery
sections.body_md: Plant and animal cells are built from the same basic parts. Both keep their DNA in a nucleus, both make proteins on ribosomes, and both run their energy supply through mitochondria.

sections.heading: What plant cells add
sections.body_md: Plant cells carry three features animal cells lack: a stiff cell wall around the outside, a large central vacuole that stores water and holds shape, and chloroplasts that capture light to make sugar.

sections.heading: Why the differences fit their lives
sections.body_md: An animal cell can move and change shape, which suits a body that hunts or travels. A plant cell stays put and builds its own food from light, so a rigid wall and light-capturing parts are worth the loss of flexibility.

key_points: Plant and animal cells share a nucleus, ribosomes, and mitochondria.
Plant cells add a cell wall, a central vacuole, and chloroplasts.
The differences match how each organism lives.
